audio.speaker_mount: Two strips of 1 mm foam double-sided tape, each about 40 x 1.5 mm, butted into one closed loop on the outer 1.5 mm of the speaker's grille face, on the collar's continuous 0.6 mm lip ring; the retainer screws press it to 0.6 mm. The tape clamps the speaker against rattle and seals the edge so the back wave cannot leak round to the front; the factory metal grille protects the cone but does neither. The loop clears all seven grille holes by about 0.8 mm (datasheet CMS-30204-18X page 2). Replaces the 1 mm foam ring (user 2026-10-14 '泡面双面胶可以试试'); no glue. Modelled as guide part speaker_tape (guide/print/world/speaker_tape.stl); the speaker model guide/print/world/speaker.stl carries the datasheet grille holes as 0.4 mm recesses.
audio.orientation: Flat metal grille with seven holes (one 7.9 mm in the middle, six 3.5 mm) towards the cap roof inside the collar; the raised 12.7 mm magnet and the two solder pads towards the retainer, pads at the end nearest the amplifier posts. Leads forward to the amplifier terminal. Figure guide/content/figures/speaker-section-{en,zh}.png, cut from the world STLs by guide/content/figures/make_speaker_section.py, shown in the guide speaker step and BRINGUP step 13 part 5.

servo_rail_7v_20261014.limits: XL4015 #1 at 7.40 V (2026-10-15): every servo holds Shutdown 52, so a reading above the Max Voltage Limit 7.0 V sets Hardware Error Status bit 0 and the Alert bit in status packets without cutting torque; overload, electrical shock and overheating still cut torque. A servo still on factory 53 latches the error and cuts torque above 7.0 V, so a fresh build writes 52 (guide step first-power) before running. guide/firmware/mac/walk_wired.py --supply auto arms its battery guard at 7.2 V, which is also what lets Alert-flagged status packets through; at 7.35 V it arms, warns under 7.0 V and stops at 6.6 V. Keep 5991 ISet closed (a 3.25 A request fails a 15 V / 3 A PDO and the board falls back to a lower voltage). Charger 15 V PDO = 45 W; about 5.5 A at 7.4 V at an assumed 90 % efficiency for servos and the head computer together, so the OpenRB DXL ports' shared 3 A rating stays the tighter limit; the 9 V PDO (27 W) is not allowed (walking_power_20261015). XL4015 module about 4 A continuous and needs its output about 1.5 V under its input. Converters are trimmed with no load and read back before J4 and the A7Z are connected.

touch_extension_20261015.user_statement_en: OK, solder the XIAO's copper-pad wires and link wires straight to its edge pads, an exception like the amplifier. Add it to the guide and run the print gate.
touch_extension_20261015.purpose: Human-pet interaction (touch, pat, stroke, hold); push from head servo current or position error. Beak grip force is a later optional extension.
touch_extension_20261015.design: Five copper foil pads on the inner face of the cap (L1, R1 18 mm; L2, R2, M 12 mm), read through the 1.7 mm PLA wall by XIAO ESP32-S3 touch pins D0, D1, D2, D3, D8. The XIAO sits on 1 mm foam tape on the inner left wall of the cap; no printed geometry changes.
touch_extension_20261015.link: I2C, XIAO as slave: D5 SCL to A7Z pin 29 (PB2), D4 SDA to pin 31 (PB3), 3V3 from pin 17, GND pin 25 (inner-row Dupont plugs). The user said 'UART'; no stock A7Z overlay serves any free inner-row pair (TWI0 overlay is CM-A7 only, corrected 2026-10-15 after the A7Z-PINS session checked compatible strings), so the four wires carry I2C under a custom overlay (TWI0 on PB2/PB3 or i2c-gpio) written and verified at the bench test, 100 kHz, internal pull-ups.
touch_extension_20261015.soldering_exception: Nine wires soldered to the XIAO edge pads (approved 2026-10-15, like the amplifier). Pad leads are also soldered to the copper pads.
touch_extension_20261015.source: guide/extension-20261015-touch/ (PLAN.md, build_touch_geometry.py, touch_routes.json); guide steps 'touch' and 'touch-pi'
touch_extension_20261015.print_gate: Passed 2026-10-15 14:4x with the parts in the guide: 176 solids closed, no unclassified overlap, 80 steps with 0 path collisions, 37 cables with no mid-route penetration. The four A7Z leads go up through the 2.3 mm gap between the plug ends and the camera board, as the amplifier BCLK wire does.
